question: Does the pinned PR #7249 token-mean normalization match an independent full-window token-mean gradient and one-step parameter update under actual two-process CPU Gloo DDP, beyond the prior single-process simulated-rank audit?

estimand.loss: For all ranks r and microbatches j in one optimizer window, L = sum_{r,j,t active} clipped_GRPO_loss(r,j,t) / sum_{r,j} active_completion_tokens(r,j).
estimand.distributed_gradient: Average the DDP-reduced per-rank gradients; compare with the gradient of the same token-mean objective on the pooled examples.
estimand.controls: No auxiliary loss, beta=0, fixed token-local CPU model, same exact multiset of samples, prompt/context positions masked from the denominator.

scope.tested_path: Pinned AsyncGRPOTrainer.compute_loss + Hugging Face Trainer/Accelerator model preparation + actual PyTorch DistributedDataParallel Gloo reducer/no_sync + manual fixed SGD parameter step.
not_tested: Finiteness of local per-sequence diagnostic ratios for a rank with zero active completion tokens; the primary finite gate covers policy loss, DDP gradients, and the SGD parameter result only.
scope.prior_evidence: The existing PR-authored tests exercise the single-process Trainer/Accelerate optimizer loop but simulate two ranks sequentially and average gradients in Python.

acceptance.any_timeout_deadlock_or_unexplained_exce: non-pass; preserve stdout/stderr and both rank exit statuses

claim_limits: This is a synthetic CPU correctness fixture under the stated token-mean contract, not a real-model or task-success result.
A passing DDP contract replay would extend distributed reducer evidence but would not establish a novel algorithm, upstream adoption, or general trainer correctness.
GRPO only; no distillation, asynchronous workers, DataloaderDispatcher, or full distributed Trainer loop is covered.
The protocol tests the objective stated in issue #7206 and PR #7249, not that token-mean weighting is the only valid objective for every use case.

In the zero-local-token case, the empty-completion rank may form 0/0 per-sequence clip diagnostics; these diagnostics are explicitly outside the acceptance gate, while global policy-loss normalization remains defined by the positive-token peer.
version_2_reason: Version 1 was interrupted before worker launch: torchrun --standalone attempted TCPStore rendezvous through reverse-resolved host 1.0.0.127.in-addr.arpa and had no worker/output after >6 minutes. This version changes only launcher rendezvous to static localhost IPv4; objective, source commits, synthetic data, metrics, thresholds, and analysis remain frozen.

launcher.reason: Avoid torchrun --standalone dynamic rendezvous resolving the loopback address to a broken reverse-DNS hostname.
